title: Wicflow Brand Film
headline: AI that moves your business forward.
subtitle: A bright, spiced-up take on the concept of the Cartesian and ClearScaler films: one isometric map of your business and its market, in Wicflow's own white, ink and service tints. The site's live-AI blue dot leaves the assistant's chat box, runs the system Wicflow builds, finds Anna's company, writes, follows up, updates the CRM, connects the tools your team uses, runs one pilot, scales it, and comes home. The business grows a floor for each tint, and the dot becomes the full stop of wicflow.com.

direction.Purpose: Show what Wicflow does in 37 seconds, for the site's hero or about section and LinkedIn; it must read with the sound off too.
direction.Audience: Owners and sales or marketing leads of growing companies in the Nordics. Not technical.
direction.Format: 16:9, 1920×1080, 30 fps, 37.5 s. ElevenLabs voice (Christina, energetic commercial), force-aligned word by word. Music and 66 effects mixed to −15 LUFS.
direction.Core message: AI that doesn't just assist but moves the business: built systems that find prospects, write, follow up and update the CRM, on the tools you already use. One pilot, measured, then scaled.
direction.Thesis: Wicflow puts AI to work across your whole business, shown on one bright map of your business and its market.
direction.Art direction: Karl's references set the concept (one isometric world, a status chip top left, captions bottom left, paths travelling the world, a scale-out, a calm logo end). The composition is our own: a loop of track round the business and five stations (market, CRM, tools, team, desk).
direction.Brand: wicflow.com measured: white paper, ink #17171B, the three service tints (blue, sage, sand) as station plates and pale washes, the live-AI blue #1769C2 only for the AI. Space Grotesk and Manrope. The traced W mark.
direction.Motion: Precise and energetic: expo-out arrivals, A1 whips for the dot between stations, A2 drop-throughs for the caption slots, small pops (8% or less) only on pills and badges. The camera only breathes. Final render with 8-sample motion blur.
direction.Transitions: Out of an object (cards grow out of the roof, drawer, plot and desk; colour fields grow out of their station), object becomes the next thing (cards fold into the dot, replies flip into Meeting booked, the tints lift into the floors, the dot becomes the full stop), and before and after on the same objects.
direction.Sound: "It's Love" by Michael Ramir C. (Mixkit, free licence), 110 BPM, fitted so the drums enter on "From finding…", the full section lands on "Less manual work" and the last chord on the end card. The effects are soft and in key, placed on each move's speed graph.

beats.title: The hook
beats.caption: What if AI didn't just assist your team, moved your business forward?
beats.idea: The AI is the site's own live dot. It lands on your business, sits beside the team as a small chat assistant (how most companies use AI), then 'assist' is struck, the bubble folds into the dot, and the dot draws a bold blue route that pulls the business forward while the market rises ahead.

revisions: Three concepts (bright world, ribbon, spiced kinetic), judged on Karl-fit, clarity and buildability
The bright world (8/10) as the spine, with the spiced concept's whips, rolls and 'Approved' pill grafted in
Closest to the references, readable in a second, buildable at polish in one session
Pale radial halos, 16 separate track plates, 15 loose logo badges; the busy check measured a median of 12 things on screen
Crisp tint plates under each station, one continuous track, the site's own tools panel; median 5 things on screen
Karl's 'too busy' lesson (K.B): fewer, bigger things
Colour stayed near-white for most of the film (under 2% saturated)
Station plates in the strongest tint stop, a blue track as the AI runs it, the found company and copies in AI blue, one full blue field
'Use their business bright colors… spice it up'
'For sales, marketing, everyday work' were three similar blooms
Each station gets an action and an upright label on its word
Each item must read in a second
'Everything connects' was a background colour change
Long blue links from the business to every station, a pulse along each
Show the verb, not a colour
Washes and the blue field swept the frame in 2–3 frames with hard edges
Feathered fields that grow out of their object over 0.6–0.8 s
The biggest frame jumps in the film
Cards popped in at full size; the message card shrank away from the dot
Every card grows out of its object; the dot holds while the card folds into it, then one long S
Every change is a move
Captions left word by word and overlapped the next line
Old line leaves as one block, gone before the next first word
Two lines of type never overlap
The building faded through, X-ray style, before the end card
It folds down solid; the disc centres on the lockup
The growth shouldn't dissolve on 'lasts'
'Wicflow helps' had no caption; the mark sat in a caption next to 'Wicflow'
The last line opens on 'Wicflow helps…'; the mark appears only in the lockup
Brand on its line; no lockup the brand doesn't use
The counter 7 → 8 had no label
'Example', as the site's demo is
Truth: the only number is illustrative
open: The full stop of wicflow.com arrives as the AI's blue dot and eases to ink for the hold. Keep it blue as a brand moment, or ink as the site's wordmark is?
The W mark is traced from the site's 384 px PNG. Ask Wicflow for the original vector before publishing.
The CRM record pairs two of the site's illustrative statuses (New contact → Interested prospect). Wicflow may prefer one verbatim row.
Music: 'It's Love' (Mixkit) is the pick. 'Motivating Mornings' (punchier) and an original composed bed are fitted too (sound/music, sound/bed_composed.wav) if Karl's ear prefers one.
The site shows the 15 tool logos the same way; check that Wicflow is fine with them in a film.
